service.name: Solo piano
service.serviceType: Solo pianist for cocktail hours, client dinners, galas and dinner parties
service.description: A solo pianist playing standards and covers at conversation volume for client dinners, galas, hotel ballroom dinners, dinner parties, Sunday brunches and memorial services across Denver, the Front Range and the Colorado mountain corridor, with a voice added when the evening wants singing.

faqs.a: Standards and covers: the Great American Songbook through the songs on the site's own list that sit under arrival and dinner, played at a level the table talks across. Tell us the evening and the set leans jazz, leans pop, or moves between the two as the night goes on, and the first learned song is included in every booking.

faqs.q: Does the venue need a piano?
faqs.a: No. When the venue has a piano, the pianist plays it. When it doesn't, a stage piano comes with the booking through the sound support every act carries, and it sets up in a 6 by 4 foot corner on one dedicated 20-amp circuit with a 45-minute load-in.

Yes. A voice joins the piano for a set or for the night when the evening wants singing, and it stays one line on the contract. On its own the piano is instrumental, which is the version most client dinners and galas book.

Conversation volume, 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table, for the whole booking. A pianist can't drift up to dance floor volume, which is the reason organisers ask for one by name for a dinner where the talking is the point.

faqs.q: Can solo piano carry a whole evening?
faqs.a: Arrival, cocktails and dinner, yes, and that is most of a client dinner or a gala. When the night wants a floor after dinner, a band or the DJ takes over on the same contract and the same sound system, so the piano is the first half of one booking rather than a separate vendor.
